When_a_HTTP_request_is_received.description: Call this to have a draft answer iteratively critiqued and revised before being returned, when output quality matters more than latency (a customer-facing answer, generated code, a structured document someone will act on). Do not use this for simple factual lookups or when speed matters more than polish — each iteration costs an additional model call and adds latency. This tool enforces a hard cap on iterations and combines an LLM judge with a deterministic check, because an LLM judge alone is not reliable enough to trust unconditionally. Read the returned 'history' field, not just 'final_answer' — it shows whether the judge and the deterministic check ever disagreed.

task.description: The task or question to answer, in full detail. This is what the model drafts an answer to on the first iteration.

draft_instructions.description: Additional constraints the draft and every revision must satisfy, e.g. 'must be under 200 words', 'must be valid JSON', 'must offer a concrete next step'. Optional but strongly recommended — the deterministic check in this tool is only as good as the constraints stated here.

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of critique-and-revise cycles. Higher costs more (each iteration is two model calls) but produces a more polished result. Optional — defaults to 3. Rarely needs to exceed 5.

score_threshold.description: Judge score from 0 to 1 at which the loop stops early and returns the current draft as final, instead of using all of max_iterations. Optional — defaults to 0.8.

variables.name: last_critique
variables.value: none yet — this is the first draft

Generate_Or_Revise_Draft.description: Verified against Microsoft's official Azure OpenAI built-in connector reference (operationId getChatCompletions, serviceProviderId /serviceProviders/openai, parameters deploymentId/messages/temperature all confirmed). If this still errors after pasting, delete it and add 'Azure OpenAI -> Get chat completions' fresh via the designer's connector picker.

messages.content: @concat('You are drafting an answer to the following task. Task: ', triggerBody()?['task'], '. Constraints: ', coalesce(triggerBody()?['draft_instructions'], 'none'), '. Previous critique to address (if any): ', variables('last_critique'), '. Previous draft (if any) to revise: ', variables('current_draft'), '. Respond with only the draft text, no preamble.')

Set_current_draft.description: Verified: 'Get chat completions' returns the generated text directly at body.content (not nested under choices[0].message.content like the raw OpenAI REST API) — confirmed against Microsoft's connector reference.

Judge_Draft.description: Same verified shape as Generate_Or_Revise_Draft above.

messages.content: @concat('Score this draft from 0 to 1 against these constraints: ', coalesce(triggerBody()?['draft_instructions'], 'general quality and relevance to: ', triggerBody()?['task']), '. Draft: ', variables('current_draft'), '. Respond with ONLY strict JSON in the form {"score": <number 0-1>, "critique": "<short text>"} and nothing else.')

Deterministic_Length_Check_Passed.description: Plain expression check, not a model call — deliberately kept separate from the judge score so a confident-but-wrong judge can't singlehandedly declare a constraint-violating draft acceptable. Extend this expression if draft_instructions implies other checkable constraints (must be valid JSON, must contain a specific keyword, etc).

Set_current_score.description: The deterministic check can only lower the judge's score, never raise it — this is the 'never trust the judge alone' principle from README.md implemented as code, not just prose.
